newsitem.title: USA: Nematron to acquire Mass. software firm.
newsitem.headline: Nematron to acquire Mass. software firm.

text.p: Nematron Corp said on Friday it signed a definitive agreement to acquire Intec Controls Corp, a Walpole, Mass.-based process control software firm, in a tax-free stock swap.
Financial details of the transaction were not disclosed.
Annual revenues of the combined companies for the last 12 months are in excess of $25 million, with more than 25 percent coming from applications software products, Nematron said.

Nematron said Intec Controls will be merged with its NemaSoft Inc subsidiary, and its products will be integrated into the current NemaSoft line of open architecture control and automation software products.

Products to be merged include client/server products and the Paragon family of high-performance regulatory control software solutions, Nematron said, adding that Intec serves a wide variety of process industries, process industries including biotechnology, chemical, food and beverage, energy and building management, pharmaceutical, textiles, and others.

NemaSoft will continue to operate the Intec unit out of its Walpole headquarters and will retain its 40 employees. It added that the Intec's software development staff will help it more rapidly develop software-based products for Microsoft Inc.'s Windows, Windows NT and for Internet and corporate intranet browser access.
